ArcelorMittal reported a group-wide LTIFR of 0.70 for 2024.

- The 2024 figure comes from the Sustainable development section of the Annual Report 2024, which states the Company LTIFR was 0.70 (alongside a fatality frequency rate of 0.03).

- This was above the yearly target of above 7.5% under normalised conditions; profitability lagged in the first half of 2024, but the strong second half brought ROIC above target (Roadmap towards 2025, evidence [1]; also Financial review, evidence [3], which notes ROIC increased to 12.3% from 7.4% in 2023).

Lerøy Havfisk's catch volume fell to 64 991 tonnes in 2024, down from 75 893 tonnes in 2023 (a decrease of about 10 902 tonnes, roughly 14%).

- The fall reflects significant quota cuts: cod reduced by 34% and haddock by 43%, plus a 6% reduction in the saithe quota in the northern zone (Results – Group, [1]).
- The quota reduction is only partly offset by higher prices, which help the trawling fleet but challenge the land-based industry, where onshore processing made a larger loss than in 2023 (Results – Group, [1]).

1st edition (1859) - elephant estimate: breeds when thirty years old, goes on breeding till ninety years old, bringing forth three pair of young in this interval; at the end of the fifth century there would be alive fifteen million elephants descended from the first pair.
6th edition (1872) - elephant estimate: begins breeding when thirty years old, goes on breeding till ninety years old, bringing forth six young in the interval, and surviving till one hundred years old; after a period of from 740 to 750 years there would be nearly nineteen million elephants alive descended from the first pair.

Between editions, Darwin changed the assumption from "three pair of young" to "six young" (the same number, reworded) and added that elephants survive till one hundred years old; the result changed from fifteen million elephants at the end of the fifth century (500 years) to nearly nineteen million elephants after 740 to 750 years.

Digital Services Act - 45 million figure: average monthly active recipients of the service in the Union, equal to or higher than 45 million (equivalent to 10 % of the Union population), calculated as an average over a period of six months.

Digital Markets Act - 45 million figure: at least 45 million monthly active end users established or located in the Union, identified and calculated in accordance with the methodology and indicators set out in the Annex (counted as unique users over a month).

Digital Markets Act - additional requirement: alongside the 45 million monthly active end users, it requires at least 10 000 yearly active business users established in the Union in the last financial year, and (for the quantitative threshold) that these thresholds were met in each of the last three financial years; for the presumption based on market capitalisation, at least EUR 75 billion in the last financial year and the same core platform service provided in at least three Member States.

The DSA counts average monthly active recipients of a service (10 % of the Union population, averaged over six months), while the DMA counts monthly active end users plus yearly active business users, so the two 45 million figures measure different things and are not directly comparable.
